sources.title: NGSS MS-LS1-3: Use argument supported by evidence for how the body is a system of interacting subsystems composed of groups of cells
OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy
OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.5 Circulatory Pathways
OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 5.1 Layers of the Skin (oxygen-poor blood is dark red)

legend.name: Oxygen-poor blood
legend.meaning: Dark red. Diagrams often use blue, but blood is never blue.

steps.title: Right side
steps.instruction: Trace the heart's right atrium and right ventricle.

note.text: The heart is two pumps side by side. The right side pumps blood to the lungs.

steps.title: Left side
steps.instruction: Trace the left atrium and left ventricle.

note.text: The left side pumps blood out to the rest of the body.

steps.title: Lungs
steps.instruction: Trace the lungs' tiny blood vessels at the top.

note.text: In the lungs, blood flows through capillaries, vessels so thin that gases pass through their walls.

steps.title: To the lungs
steps.instruction: Draw the vessel from the right ventricle up to the lungs.

note.text: The pulmonary artery carries oxygen-poor blood to the lungs, where it drops carbon dioxide and picks up oxygen.

steps.title: Back from the lungs
steps.instruction: Draw the vessel from the lungs to the left atrium.

note.text: Pulmonary veins bring the oxygen-rich blood back to the heart. This loop is the pulmonary circuit.

steps.title: Body
steps.instruction: Trace the body's capillaries at the bottom.

note.text: In the body's capillaries, oxygen and food pass out to the cells, and waste like carbon dioxide passes in.

steps.title: Aorta
steps.instruction: Draw the aorta from the left ventricle down to the body.

note.text: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. The aorta, the biggest, carries oxygen-rich blood to the body.

steps.title: Vena cava
steps.instruction: Draw the vena cava from the body back to the right atrium.

note.text: Veins carry blood back to the heart. This loop through the body is the systemic circuit.

steps.title: Color
steps.instruction: Color the heart's two sides and the lungs. Oxygen-poor blood is dark red; oxygen-rich is bright red.

steps.title: One full trip
steps.instruction: Tap the stops in order, starting at the right ventricle.
steps.why: Blood makes two loops: right side to the lungs and back to the left side, then left side to the body and back.
steps.hint: Where does blood pick up oxygen?

steps.title: Systems working together
steps.question: How do the circulatory and respiratory systems work together?

options.text: The lungs take in oxygen, and the blood carries it to every cell
options.feedback: Yes. Neither system could keep cells alive alone: one gets oxygen in, the other delivers it.
They depend on each other. Blood must pass through the lungs to pick up oxygen.

options.text: The heart breathes for the lungs
options.feedback: The heart pumps blood; the lungs exchange gases. Together they supply oxygen.
The heart pumps blood. The lungs are where oxygen enters it.

steps.title: Strong side
steps.question: Why does the left ventricle need a thicker, stronger wall than the right?

options.text: It pumps blood all around the body, not just next door to the lungs
options.feedback: Right. The systemic circuit is far longer than the trip to the lungs, so it needs much more force.
Wall thickness is about pumping force. The left ventricle pushes blood around the whole body.

options.text: It pumps blood to the lungs
options.feedback: That's the right ventricle's job. The left pumps to the whole body.

options.text: It doesn't: both are the same
options.feedback: The left ventricle's wall is much thicker, because it pumps to the whole body.
